reason: E1 directly supports the mechanism linking nanohierarchical structure to adaptive wear protection and ultralow wear from RT to 800 °C, but it concerns a different alloy system (Ni50(AlNbTiV)50) and does not provide evidence that a small Ti addition to CoCrFeNi will produce the required nanoprecipitate dispersion or glaze layer. E2 addresses W addition in AlCoCrFeNi coatings and does not support the specific claims about Ti-induced nanoprecipitation or adaptive glaze formation in CoCrFeNi. Thus, the core premises about the intervention's effect on CoCrFeNi are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Nanohierarchical architecture with nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates yields ultralow wear from RT to 800 °C in a complex concentrated alloy
This structure enables multi-type adaptive friction interface protection, releasing gradient frictional stress at RT and forming a nanocrystalline glaze layer at 800 °C
A small reactive addition (Ti) to CoCrFeNi can induce in-situ formation of finely dispersed nanoprecipitates and a nanohierarchical microstructure
The Ti-rich nanoprecipitates will oxidize at high temperature to form a dense, lubricious nanocrystalline glaze layer
This dual-phase structure will lower both COF and wear rate across the full RT–800 °C range relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi
